# `silk/geometry/rounded_rect`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Axis-aligned rectangles with a circular radius at each corner, over any number type.

## When to use
Use [`RoundedRect`](#RoundedRect) for the outline of a card, a button, a shadow, or a clip with rounded
corners. Use `silk.geometry.rect.Rect` when every corner is square.

## Details
A rounded rectangle is a `Copy` struct with the public fields `rect`, a
`silk.geometry.rect.Rect`, and `radii`, a `silk.geometry.corners.Corners`, both of number type
`T`. Each corner is a quarter circle whose radius is the matching field of `radii`. Radii are
stored as given; [`clampRadii`](#RoundedRect.impl.clampRadii) fits them to the rectangle. `&a == &b` compares the rectangle
and every radius when `T: Equal`.

## Gotchas
[`contains`](#RoundedRect.impl.contains) assumes the radii already fit: none is negative and none exceeds half the smaller
side. Call [`clampRadii`](#RoundedRect.impl.clampRadii) first when the radii come from user input or a style.

## Examples
### Hit-test a rounded button
```silk
import silk.geometry.point { Point2 }
import silk.geometry.rect { Rect }
import silk.geometry.rounded_rect { RoundedRect }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let button = RoundedRect<f64>.uniform(Rect<f64>.new(0.0, 0.0, 120.0, 40.0), 10.0)
  if !button.contains(Point2<f64>.new(60.0, 20.0)) || button.contains(Point2<f64>.new(1.0, 1.0)) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `RoundedRect` with `import silk.geometry.rounded_rect { RoundedRect }`.

## `RoundedRect`

```silk
pub struct RoundedRect<T>
```

An axis-aligned rectangle of number type `T` with a circular radius at each corner.

### When to use

Use `RoundedRect` for rounded boxes such as cards, buttons, shadows, and clips. Use
`silk.geometry.rect.Rect` when every corner is square.

### Details

The fields are public. Each corner is a quarter circle whose radius is the matching field of
`radii`; a zero radius gives a square corner. Radii are stored as given, so they can be negative
or larger than the rectangle until [`clampRadii`](#RoundedRect.impl.clampRadii) fits them. `&a == &b` compares the rectangle
and every radius when `T: Equal`.

<a id="RoundedRect.rect"></a>


The bounds of the shape, with inclusive edges.

<a id="RoundedRect.radii"></a>

### Field `radii`

```silk
pub radii: Corners<T>
```

The radius at each corner, with top at the minimum y edge and left at the minimum x edge.

<a id="RoundedRect.impl.clampRadii"></a>

### Method `clampRadii`

```silk
pub fn clampRadii(self: Self) -> RoundedRect<T>
```

Returns the rounded rectangle with its radii fitted to its size: each radius is clamped
between zero and half of the smaller of the width and the height.

#### Details

Each corner is clamped on its own, as GPU quad shaders do, so a fitted corner keeps its radius
even when another corner is reduced. A reversed or zero-area rectangle gets zero radii. The
rectangle itself is unchanged.

<a id="RoundedRect.impl.contains"></a>

### Method `contains`

```silk
pub fn contains(self: &Self, point: Point2<T>) -> bool
```

Returns `true` when `point` is inside the shape or on its outline.

#### Details

A point is inside when it is inside `rect`, edges included, and not outside the quarter
circle of the corner it falls in. A point exactly on a corner arc is inside.

#### Gotchas

The radii must already fit: none negative and none above half the smaller side. Call
[`clampRadii`](#RoundedRect.impl.clampRadii) first when they may not, or the corner regions overlap and the answer is not
meaningful. For an integer type, the squared distances can overflow for coordinates near the
type's limit.
